elements.element: Customer may terminate the Agreement or an Order Form for convenience.
elements.evidence: Rendered 14.2.2: "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ". The $60 million Development Cost condition precedent and the "prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval" cut-off are struck, so the election is unconditional. This Agreement has no Order Form structure, so the Agreement-level right suffices. (The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present: false" is a false negative on this text \u2014 the express words "terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause" appear in the operative sentence.)

elements.element: Customer's convenience termination requires no more than 30 days' written notice.
elements.evidence: "upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to SFJ" \u2014 the blank [***] notice figure in the original is replaced with a fixed 30-day written notice, which is at the preferred ceiling.

elements.element: Vendor refunds prepaid fees pro rata after Customer's convenience termination.
elements.evidence: "and SFJ will refund pro rata any fees or other amounts prepaid by PB for the period after the effective date of termination" \u2014 the word "pro rata" is express (not merely inferred from a post-termination period), the payer is the Vendor (SFJ) and the trigger is PB's convenience termination under 14.2.2.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: "SFJ has no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term." "Term" is a defined concept (1.1.185 / Section 14.1). The retained SFJ exits are each trigger-conditioned rather than at-will \u2014 14.2.6 requires a Change of Control of PB and 14.2.10 requires PB's exercise of Section 5.2.4 authority plus continued good-faith JSC disagreement \u2014 so the new sentence does not contradict them. 14.2.10 is discretionary-in-substance once its trigger fires, but its trigger is a real condition, so the element is satisfied on the operative text.

elements.element: Customer may terminate for convenience on 60 to 90 days' notice.
elements.evidence: The rendered notice period is thirty (30) days, which is below (and therefore outside) the 60\u201390 day fallback band. Not a defect \u2014 the proposal targets the preferred level \u2014 but the fallback element as literally stated is not met.

elements.element: Any early-termination fee is capped at three months of fees.
elements.evidence: The redline retains the sentence requiring PB to pay "an amount equal to three hundred percent (300%) of Development Costs paid or incurred by SFJ prior to such termination", plus continuing ARTICLE 6 Approval Payments. There is no three-months-of-fees cap and no fee concept to measure one against.

elements.element: Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term.
elements.evidence: The inserted sentence bars SFJ convenience termination for the whole Term, which is at least as protective as confining it to term end; no SFJ at-will right survives in the retained text (14.2.6 and 14.2.10 are trigger-based).

elements.element: Vendor must give at least 90 days' notice of convenience termination.
elements.evidence: Conditional element whose condition does not arise: because the redline gives SFJ no convenience termination right during the Term, there is no Vendor convenience notice to regulate.

elements.element: Vendor has no right to terminate for convenience during a committed term.
elements.evidence: Duplicated for completeness of the fallback picture: the express sentence "SFJ has no right to terminate this Agreement for convenience during the Term" also satisfies the fallback's Vendor-side restriction.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: all four preferred elements are met in operative language (unconditional PB convenience right, 30 days' written notice, express pro rata refund of prepayments, express bar on SFJ convenience termination during the Term). Nothing is merely promised in the margin comment.

The deterministic check "Customer convenience termination present = false" is a false negative; the rendered clause contains the express grant "PB may terminate this Agreement for convenience, without cause, at any time upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice". Substantive inspection controls.

Fallback is not satisfied (30-day notice sits outside the 60\u201390 day band and the retained 300%-of-Development-Costs payment is uncapped), but that is immaterial because the preferred checklist is complete.

Minimality holds: the deletions are confined to the three defects that blocked the element set \u2014 the $60 million Development Cost gate, the first-Regulatory-Approval cut-off, and the blank [***] notice figure. The two inserted sentences map one-to-one to the refund and no-Vendor-convenience elements. Model-language surplus "in whole or in part" was correctly dropped (no Order Form or partial-termination structure here), and the 300% Trial Data Package consideration, the ARTICLE 6 Approval Payment carry-over, Section 6.2 adjustment and Section 6.7 credit are all left intact. "without cause, at any time" is mildly redundant of "for convenience" but adds no requirement outside the checklist.

Broadening the refund from "fees" to "any fees or other amounts prepaid by PB" is justified rather than gold-plating: the Agreement has no defined fee concept and uses Approval Payments / Buy-Out Payment, so a fee-only refund would be an undefined trigger.

Intent is preserved: 14.2.6 (Change of Control) and 14.2.10 (JSC decision) are untouched and remain trigger-conditioned, so they do not contradict the new no-convenience sentence; no cross-reference is left dangling and "Term" is defined at 1.1.185.

Actionable residual (drafting hygiene, not an element failure): by removing the "prior to the date of receipt of the first Regulatory Approval" limit, PB may now terminate after Approval, yet the retained sentence is framed as "if PB elects to continue development of the Product and obtains Regulatory Approval following such termination". Consider adding "or has obtained Regulatory Approval prior to such termination" so the ARTICLE 6 carry-over is not left silent for a post-Approval exit.

Actionable residual: the exit is unconditional but not free \u2014 the retained 300% Development Cost payment plus continuing Approval Payments means PB's convenience exit carries substantial cost. If the playbook's "without penalty" objective is to bite, the negotiating ask should be an express statement that the 300% amount is consideration for the Trial Data Package and is waivable if PB declines to purchase it; that is a separate commercial point and is correctly flagged rather than redlined.
